symptom_short: A restarted ZooKeeper observer never syncs with the leader: every sync attempt dies with a NullPointerException while it is rolling its transaction log back, the member loops forever re-electing and retrying, and each attempt leaks its leader connection (sockets pile up in CLOSE_WAIT until connections fail)

milestones.note: Folder scaffolded (private/ source/ logs/ diagnosis/); PROGRESS.md + state.json created; bug claimed in COORDINATION.log.

JIRA ZOOKEEPER-1900 'NullPointerException in truncate' (Blocker, affects 3.4.5/3.4.6, fixVersion 3.4.7+3.5.0, Resolved/Fixed; reported by Camille Fournier). Ticket quotes the stack frame 'java.lang.NullPointerException at org.apache.zookeeper.server.persistence.FileTxnLog.truncate(FileTxnLog.java:352)' and the message 'Truncating log to get in sync with the leader', repeated >1M times/day, plus ~29k sockets stuck in CLOSE_WAIT until new connections failed with ConnectException. Fix commit (trunk/3.5.0) = 6abd85938 (Alexander Shraer, 2014-06-30, svn trunk@1606841); companion branch-3.4 commit 8ff14a712 saved as private/fix.branch-3.4.diff. Trunk diff changes exactly two production lines: (1) FileTxnLog.truncate() gains 'if (input == null) throw new IOException("No log files found to truncate! ...")' before 'long pos = input.getPosition();' and (2) Observer.observeLeader()'s inner 'catch (IOException e)' becomes 'catch (Exception e)'; it also adds TruncateTest.testTruncationNullLog. The branch-3.4 diff is identical plus the same catch widening in Follower.java (trunk's Follower already caught Exception). pre_fix_commit = 8cfb9a0ef (ZOOKEEPER-1576, 2014-06-27) - verified its FileTxnLog.truncate does 'PositionInputStream input = itr.inputStream; long pos = input.getPosition();' with no null guard, and FileTxnIterator.init() leaves inputStream null when the log directory contains no log.* file (storedFiles stays empty so goToNextLog() returns false). Confirmed the diff resolves the reported symptom: a learner told to TRUNC whose dataLogDir holds no txn log NPEs inside truncate; on an observer the NPE (a RuntimeException) escapes the 'catch (IOException)' in observeLeader, so sock.close() never runs (CLOSE_WAIT leak) and the exception unwinds to QuorumPeer.run, which drops the peer back to LOOKING and retries forever.

Built the pre-fix tree (8cfb9a0ef, ZooKeeper 3.5.0-SNAPSHOT) from source with Ant+Ivy in per-bug image clods-eval:Zookeeper-Zookeeper-1900 (clods-eval base + openjdk-8-jdk + ant + ant-optional; JDK 11/17 refuse -source/-target < 7). Build cmd: 'ant jar' -> build/zookeeper-3.5.0-SNAPSHOT.jar + build/classes + build/lib (slf4j 1.7.5, log4j 1.2.16, jline 2.11, netty 3.7.0.Final, commons-cli 1.2). Dep fixes (private/deps-fix.patch, 3 edits, no source changes; identical to the ones another agent needed for the neighbouring 2014 trunk commit): (1) build.xml ivy.url http://repo2.maven.org -> https://repo1.maven.org (repo2 host is gone and Central refuses plain HTTP); (2) build.xml javac.source/javac.target 1.5 -> 1.8 (javac 8 rejects source/target 1.5 with its 1.8 bootclasspath); (3) ivysettings.xml repo.maven.org/repo.jboss.org/repo.sun.org -> https://repo1.maven.org (jboss nexus + download.java.net are dead). BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 7s, 4 rawtypes warnings only.

Reproduced on the real system: a 4-member ZooKeeper 3.5.0-SNAPSHOT ensemble built from the pre-fix tree (myid 1-3 participants, myid 4 peerType=observer), all four with root logger AND console appender at DEBUG, snapshots (dataDir) and transaction logs (dataLogDir) on separate directories, roles discovered with the servers' own 'srvr' 4lw. PHASE A (previous deployment): six concurrent Workload clients x 280 create/getData/setData/exists/getChildren/delete iterations spread over all three participants, a real zkCli shell session on the leader (40x create/get/set/stat + 20 deletes) and a client doing ephemeral work through the observer -> ~4000 txns; the observer ends with 18 snapshots + 18 txn logs, newest snapshot.100000fc6. All members stopped. PHASE B (operator action, no code touched): the three participants are re-provisioned on empty storage; the observer keeps its dataDir and its dataLogDir is repointed at a new EMPTY directory - the exact situation the upstream fix's own message names ('snapshots from an old setup ... or dataLogDir was changed in zoo.cfg'). PHASE C (incident): the re-provisioned quorum comes up at epoch 1 (leader zxid 0x1000003b0) and serves real traffic (2x120-iteration workloads + a client doing 185 ops over the 40s window, 0 failures). The observer starts, reports its snapshot zxid 0x100000fc6 (far ahead), the leader logs 'Synchronizing with Follower sid: 4 maxCommittedLog=0x100000269 ... peerLastZxid=0x100000fc6' and 'Sending TRUNC to follower', and the observer dies with java.lang.NullPointerException at FileTxnLog.truncate:381 <- FileTxnSnapLog.truncateLog:317 <- ZKDatabase.truncateLog:504 <- Learner.syncWithLeader:348 <- Observer.observeLeader:79 <- QuorumPeer.run:961, then 'shutdown called' -> PeerState LOOKING -> OBSERVING -> same failure, 6239 times in 40s. It never serves a client (srvr: 'This ZooKeeper instance is not currently serving requests'; an ordinary client gets connect=TIMEOUT after 20s in CONNECTING) and it leaks one leader connection per attempt (observer sockets 25 -> 122, CLOSE_WAIT 0 -> 42). Detection is silent: assertions read the servers' own logs, the clients' result files and /proc, and print only to reproduce.sh stdout. Workload.java writes nothing to stdout/stderr; NO log or print statement was added to ZooKeeper anywhere. private/symptom.orig.log = 524674 lines / 75 MB (241073 DEBUG, 119743 INFO, 31333 WARN/ERROR) = 8 server logs (previous deployment + current) + 13 client session logs, one '===== file: X =====' header each. Attempt 1 (identical scenario, 2 clients x 700 ops, 70s window) also reproduced (11276 NPEs); it was re-run only to keep each client's request xid below 1900 and to halve the log size. || M3 EXTENDED 2026-08-16 for the new METHODOLOGY §5/M3 step 8 (merge the reproduction into the system's production log). The reproduction itself is unchanged (same script, same run, same private/symptom.orig.log = Log A). Added: the shared read-only production-logs/Zookeeper/production.log (1.5 GB, 8052741 records, 7-node ensemble under YCSB + chaos monkey, span 2026-08-14 18:44:25,716 .. 19:28:51,007) is merged with Log A by private/merge_logs.py -> private/merged.orig.log (Log B): 8052741 production + 392149 reproduction records, 1.6 GB, in 63 s. Retime-don't-rewrite: only each reproduction record's leading timestamp is linearly warped from the reproduction span (2026-08-12 18:01:31,351 .. 18:02:52,935) onto the full production span; every other character of every line is verbatim. --interleave position (not the spec's literal timestamp merge) because this production log is a bundle of 10 concatenated per-host sections (zk1..zk7 + rotations), each restarting the clock over the same window, so a timestamp merge would collapse the whole reproduction into the first section - the opposite of the spec's 'spread across the production timeline' requirement; position interleaving keeps the retiming rule and only changes the insertion key. merge_logs.py is Zookeeper-1851's tool copied verbatim (unmodified) so both ZooKeeper bugs merge identically; the shared production log is never modified.

Minimal, case-targeted anonymization. Renamed exactly one distinctive vocabulary - the transaction-log TRUNCATION terms that name the ticket ('NullPointerException in truncate', whose report quotes the frame FileTxnLog.truncate(FileTxnLog.java:352) and the message 'Truncating log to get in sync with the leader'): truncate->rollBack, truncateLog->rollBackLog, truncated->rolledBack, truncating/truncation->rolling back/roll-back, Leader.TRUNC (int 14) + its "TRUNC" packet-name string->ROLLBACK, TruncateTest.java->RollBackTest.java. The two ticket-quoted log messages were rewritten at the source, so the binaries emit 'Rolling back the transaction log to get in sync with the leader' and the stack frame reads FileTxnLog.rollBack(FileTxnLog.java:381) - same line, renamed method (the ticket's :352 is the 3.4.5 line). Everything else stays real: packages, all other class names, leader/follower/observer/learner/quorum/znode/zxid/epoch/snapshot terminology, every other log message, the NullPointerException type and full stack shape, version 3.5.0-SNAPSHOT. The renamed tree was REBUILT ('ant jar', BUILD SUCCESSFUL) at the NEUTRAL path repos/zookeeper-ensemble-src (the JVM prints user.dir + the classpath into every log, so a path naming the bug leaked '1900' 40+ times in the M3 log) and reproduce.sh was re-run against it, so logs/symptom.log (512839 lines / 74 MB) is the genuine output of the renamed binaries, not a rewritten log: the failure reproduces identically (6058 NPEs in 40s at FileTxnLog.rollBack:381, observer snapshot 0x100001013 vs leader 0x1000003b2, srvr 'not currently serving requests', client connect=TIMEOUT, observer sockets 35->113, CLOSE_WAIT 0->32). source/ = the full renamed pre-fix Java tree (282 files: src/java/main + src/java/generated), not a hand-curated subset, so no file-selection hint is given to the LLM. Verified on the host: 0 hits for ZOOKEEPER-1900, bare \b1900\b, [Tt]runcat and \bTRUNC\b across source/ + logs/symptom.log + symptom.md. Attempts 1-2 failed on the built-in checks (rename missed 3 files' comments/test-class name; then two reproduce.sh assertions still grepped the old vocabulary) and were re-run - no artifact from them was kept.

REDONE under the updated context/METHODOLOGY.md §5/M5 (commits 466a79e/ebba23d/8d90c20: 'symptom.md = bare observable + log pointer, nothing else'). The first version of symptom.md violated the new rule: it narrated the JIRA-style trigger and timeline (maintenance window, three participants re-provisioned on empty storage, the fourth member's transaction-log directory repointed at a replacement volume), described the mechanism (never rejoins, falls back to leader election, retries), and added the narrowing comparisons 'the quorum is healthy and serves clients' and the growing CLOSE_WAIT socket count. All of that is cause, not symptom, so it was deleted. New symptom.md = two sentences ('One member of the ZooKeeper ensemble is not serving client requests. Its log for this run, logs/symptom.log, repeats the following thousands of times (first at line 244231):') followed by the exception exactly as the log prints it at line 244231 - the QuorumPeer@963 'Unexpected exception' WARN plus the six-frame java.lang.NullPointerException trace (FileTxnLog.rollBack:381 <- FileTxnSnapLog.rollBackLog:317 <- ZKDatabase.rollBackLog:504 <- Learner.syncWithLeader:348 <- Observer.observeLeader:79 <- QuorumPeer.run:961), copied from the log and NOT from the JIRA attachment. ground_truth.md keeps the same two required sites (A: the unguarded itr.inputStream dereference at FileTxnLog.rollBack 380-381 plus the exact null-ness condition; B: Observer.observeLeader's catch (IOException e) at line 85), but B's justification was restated: naming the CLOSE_WAIT consequence is no longer required (it left the symptom), and B is required because the fix touched it (§10) and because the pasted trace's top frame QuorumPeer.run:961 under 'Unexpected exception' is itself proof the handler at Observer.java:85 did not apply to a RuntimeException. M5 verification gate re-run: 0 hits for ZOOKEEPER-1900, \b1900\b, [Tt]runcat and \bTRUNC\b across source/ + logs/symptom.log + symptom.md; sentence-by-sentence audit finds no trigger, no mechanism/timeline, no at-fault component/branch, no narrowing comparison, no JIRA narrative. source/ and logs/symptom.log are unchanged (M2-M4 stand); only the LLM-facing symptom text changed, so M6-M8 were discarded and re-run.

RE-RUN against the rewritten (bare-observable) symptom.md. 5 independent single-turn diagnoses, model claude-opus-4-7 effort high, egress iptables-locked to api.anthropic.com:443 (--add-host pins 160.79.104.10 so the lock survives the DNS-killing DROP policy), Bash/Write/Edit/WebFetch/WebSearch/Task/NotebookEdit denied, --safe-mode --no-session-persistence --exclude-dynamic-system-prompt-sections, no follow-up prompts, throwaway staging dir holding ONLY source/ + logs/symptom.log + symptom.md (verified at runtime: 'ls -A' on the stage shows exactly logs/ source/ symptom.md, and the prompt's symptom text is the new two-sentence + pasted-stack version). Same harness deviation as before and as recorded for Zookeeper-1851: the image's baked-in /opt/clods/run_diagnosis.sh is stale, so context/ was mounted read-only and the tracked context/run_diagnosis.sh executed instead; context/ and the image were NOT modified. Host CCS OAuth credentials were copied into a scratch config dir (CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR + IS_SANDBOX=1 + CLAUDE_PURITY_FLAG=--safe-mode) and deleted afterwards. All 5 runs completed first time, all 5 stderr files empty, answers 3.5-4.8 kB. source/ and logs/symptom.log are byte-identical to the M4 artifacts - only the symptom text differs from the discarded batch.

0/5 PASS under the pre-registered two-site rule. The five runs are remarkably uniform: EVERY run nailed site A - the unguarded 'PositionInputStream input = itr.inputStream; long pos = input.getPosition();' at FileTxnLog.rollBack 380-381 - together with the exact branch condition that makes it null (no log.* file in the txnlog dir -> FileTxnIterator.init leaves storedFiles empty -> goToNextLog()'s 'if (storedFiles.size() > 0)' is false -> createInputArchive(), the only assignment of inputStream, is never called), and four of them stated the missing guard or the one-line fix explicitly. Runs 1, 3 and 5 additionally derived a correct SECOND route to the same null (fast-forward hitting EOF, where next() nulls inputStream and goToNextLog() then returns false) that the upstream patch's own null check also covers. NONE of the five named site B: not one mentions Observer.java:85, the 'catch (IOException e)' in Observer.observeLeader, or the fact that a NullPointerException is a RuntimeException the handler cannot match. All five instead credit the repetition to QuorumPeer.run's broad 'catch (Exception e)' (962-963) - a correct account of the repetition (the peer re-enters OBSERVING even with a widened handler) but not a line the fix changed. This is a direct consequence of the tightened M5 symptom: the discarded batch, whose symptom.md mentioned sockets piling up in CLOSE_WAIT, scored 5/5 with every run naming Observer.java:85; with the socket observable removed, nothing in the stated symptom motivates the exception-handling site and no run went looking for it. Recorded verdicts follow METHODOLOGY §10 ('the fix touches multiple files/branches: ... a run must name all to PASS') and §8 (no partial credit). Each grade JSON carries site_a/site_b fields so the alternative bar - root-causing line only - is auditable: that bar would score 5/5.

0/5 PASS under the two-site bar; 5/5 on the root-causing line alone. summary.md records the comparison that makes this re-run informative: the discarded batch's symptom.md still mentioned the CLOSE_WAIT socket growth and all five of those runs found Observer.java:85; with that single observable removed - source/ and logs/symptom.log byte-identical - no run looked at exception handling at all. The model's search is symptom-driven, not fix-driven: it explains exactly what it is asked to explain and does not audit surrounding code for related defects. summary.md also keeps the standing caveat that this is a fail-stop bug whose stack trace names the guilty frame 6058 times, so it is weak evidence for the CLODS argument either way, and states plainly that a two-site bar on a patch whose second site the symptom does not exhibit measures the symptom's coverage as much as the model's reasoning - both numbers are recorded so the operator can choose the bar.

result.note: 0/5 under the pre-registered two-site bar (both lines the fix changed). All 5 runs identified the root-causing line and its branch condition (site A); none identified the catch-widening site (Observer.java:85). Under a root-causing-line-only bar the score would be 5/5. The earlier 5/5 batch was produced against a cause-leaking symptom.md and is discarded.
